title: dynamic batching: refine sequence-length bucketing to minimize padding and improve latency
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: the existing dynamic-batching-by-seqlen logic used coarse buckets which increased padding for mid-length requests and reduced GPU utilization during mixed workloads. This PR implements a finer-grained bucketing heuristic and an adaptive padding floor to reduce wasted tokens while keeping dispatch latency within SLOs. Key changes: 1) introduce percentile-driven bucket boundaries computed from sliding window traffic stats; 2) add a cost model that trades off additional batching delay vs expected padding overhead to decide whether to wait for more compatible requests; 3) integrate bucket-aware kernel selection so that padded batches pick kernels optimized for the resulting effective sequence length; 4) KV-cache compatibility: preserve cache shard affinity when re-bucketing to avoid cold-cache penalties; 5) metrics and benchmarks for continuous-batching under mixed seqlen distributions. This description includes rationale, rollout plan, and test summary. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-8971) [x] unit tests covering bucketing logic [x] integration tests for end-to-end throughput/lossless output [x] benchmark harness results attached [x] feature gated behind runtime config and rollout flag. Rollout plan: enable in canary for 24h with traffic shadowing then staged global rollout with automatic rollback if p99 latency regresses >6%.

release_notes: Improves dynamic batching heuristics by grouping requests into finer sequence-length buckets and introducing an adaptive padding floor. Expected improvements: lower padding overhead, better GPU utilization, and reduced p90/p99 latency in mixed workload traffic. Feature is gated behind a runtime flag and rolled out gradually.
change_summary: Finer-grained sequence-length bucketing, adaptive padding decision model, bucket-aware kernel selection, KV-cache shard-affinity preservation, telemetry and tests.
performance_results: p90 latency: -12% on mixed short/long workload (canary)
token cost per request: -9% estimated in bench harness
notes: This PR is part of the ENG-8971 initiative to reduce per-token serving cost across mixed seqlen workloads. The runtime flag 'dyn_batch_v4' controls behavior and defaults to off; operators should enable in canary before global rollout.
ephemeral_risks: Potential risk: if bucket boundaries are tuned too aggressively the scheduler may wait and increase tail latency for strict low-latency customers. Mitigation: per-customer config and automatic fallback to current algorithm when latency SLOs are threatened.
observability_changes: Added metrics: runtime.dyn_batch.bucket_count, runtime.dyn_batch.padded_tokens_saved, runtime.dyn_batch.wait_decisions, runtime.dyn_batch.kv_affinity_rebalances; dashboards updated in docs/operational/dynamic_batching.md
testing_summary: Unit tests cover bucket estimator, cost model, and atomic updates. Integration tests validate end-to-end correctness (outputs identical). Benchmarks run with mixed_seqlen harness comparing v3 vs v4 heuristics; results attached in PR artifacts.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature-flag for 5% traffic in canary, monitor metrics for 24h, then staged ramp by 2x every 12h until full rollout or rollback on regression.
